group:paper-gaokao-2022-zhejiang-jun:sev.overview: 以孩子给圣诞老人写信为例，说明写作应有真实目的，并随读者和情境调整语言；从家人称呼延伸到即时通信与正式写作的差异。
group:paper-gaokao-2022-zhejiang-jun:sev.fullTranslationZh:
我有一抽屉写给圣诞老人的信。每年孩子们都会写下圣诞愿望清单，礼貌地请求最新的游戏或玩具。随着年龄增长，他们还会提示圣诞老人到哪里买礼物。因此，他们每年都收到了自己想要的东西。

这些信让孩子学到一条宝贵的写作道理：写作有目的。有时是为了达成某件事，有时是为了娱乐、告知或说服。但写作总是有目的的，至少应该如此。当写作似乎毫无目的，也得不到任何有意义的回应时，人就很难对它感到兴奋。

圣诞节是孩子通过写作与别人交流的好时机。当孩子为真实读者、真实目的写作时，就能学会相应选择措辞。你会写“嗨，奶奶和爷爷”，因为你们很亲近；你写“亲爱的圣诞老人”，则因为你与他不熟悉，想表示尊重。

随着技术发展，年轻人比过去任何时候都写得更多。短信、网络消息、玩电子游戏时实时聊天，都意味着他们不断产生书面消息。不过，由于通常是在给家人和朋友写，他们大多使用非正式语言。

这种写作本身没有问题。它适合读者与目的，也完成了任务。但如果这是年轻人唯一会做的写作，就会产生问题。这种写作不会获得学校阅卷者、未来雇主或潜在客户的认可。最出色的沟通者懂得调整语言，使之适合读者。

completedSourceTexts.text: I have a drawer full of letters to Santa. Each year my children would write up their Christmas wish lists. They were polite requests for the latest game or toy. As the children got older, they would give Santa some hints(提示)on where to buy their presents. As a result, each year they received something they wanted.

Those letters taught my children a valuable lesson about writing: It has a purpose. Sometimes our purpose is to achieve something; other times it may be to entertain, inform, or persuade. But it is always purposeful-or at least it should be. And when writing doesn’t seem to have any purpose or get any kind of meaningful response, then it can be hard to get excited about doing it.

Christmas is a great time of year for children to communicate with others through writing. When children write for real audiences and real purposes, they can learn to choose their words accordingly. You write “Hi Nanna and Pop” because you are close to them. You write “Dear Santa” because you don’t know him personally and you want to show him respect.

As technology develops, young people are writing more than they ever have. Texting, online messaging, live chats while playing video games all mean that they are constantly producing written messages. However, because they are usually writing to family and friends, they use informal language most of the time.

There is nothing wrong with this kind of writing. It suits the audience and the purpose and gets the job done. But if this is the only kind of writing young people do, it will cause problems. This type of writing won’t be rewarded by the school examiner, nor by a future employer or a potential client. The very best communicators are those who know how to adjust their language to match their audience.
